decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: spec lists 'automatic title/icon fetching as out of scope for now' (client paraphrase confirms maker's presentation excluded auto-metadata). Round 1 client: 'I'd really like to just paste a web address and have the app fill in the page's name for me, instead of typing a title every time... I saw you've listed automatic title/icon fetching as out of scope for now — I can live with entering titles myself to get started, but I'd like it noted as something I want soon.'
decisions.note: Spec-review stage. Reference REF-BM-02 requires auto-collecting title/description/favicon/preview on save; presentation put this out of scope, a real divergence. The client explicitly states the expected behaviour (paste URL, app fills the name) and identifies the difference, then explicitly accepts the departure ('I can live with entering titles myself to get started'), asking only that it be noted for later rather than aligned now. Matches the accepted_divergence pattern; catch_type=none. Reaffirmed at round 2 ('glad the automatic title lookup is written down as the next thing to add') — same decision, counted once.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker presented 'Validation and duplicate prevention' as delivered. Round 4 client (implementation review): 'When I try to save a link that's already in my collection, instead of telling me it's already saved and taking me to the existing one, it shows an error that says the bookmark "could not be saved, please try again."... Please fix that so re-saving a link I already have quietly points me to the existing bookmark rather than showing a failure message.' Round 5 maker fixed it; round 5 client confirmed it now keeps the single bookmark and announces 'Already saved — taking you to it.'
decisions.note: Implementation-review stage. Reference REF-BM-06 requires re-saving an existing url to guide the user to edit the existing bookmark, not create a new one / not fail. The implementation diverged (generic failure message). The client rejected the mismatch and supplied the reference-conforming behaviour (point to the existing bookmark), so catch_type=correct. Round 5 re-presentation now conforms; confirmation is disposition of the same decision, not double-counted.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Clear MVP exclusions such as sharing, imports, folders, extensions, and offline use.' Round 1 client responds to auto-title fetching and general approval but never mentions imports; no later mention across rounds 2-5.
decisions.note: Spec-review stage. Reference REF-BM-30 requires import of bookmarks in Netscape HTML format; the presentation explicitly excluded 'imports', an established divergence. The client's response neither corrects it nor expresses the difference — it passes on general approval, so unexpressed_divergence, caught=false.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Saving and opening bookmarks'; round 4 maker: 'Save and open bookmarks', 'Selecting a list item navigates to the original url' implied by opening. Round 4 client: 'I signed in, saved links with tags, opened my list... all smooth.'
decisions.note: Recorded in-scope decision conforming to reference (save by URL, open original). Presented and confirmed; not a divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Editing'; round 4 maker: 'Bookmark editing'. Round 4 client: 'edited a bookmark... all smooth.'
decisions.note: Conforming presented decision for editing a bookmark; no divergence from REF-BM-04.

decisions.note: Conforming presented decision for delete (with confirmation); REF-BM-05 satisfied, not divergent.

decisions.note: Conforming presented decision for assigning tags and filtering by a tag (REF-BM-09, REF-BM-11); no divergence surfaced.
